narrative.overview: The Unifesto app is a student's pocket to the whole fest circuit — discover events, hold tickets and QR codes, top up a wallet, refer friends, chat, and pay. It lives on a true-black canvas that reads as premium and AI-native, letting the Unifesto blue gradient glow like neon. Where the dashboards work in daylight, the app performs at night: high-contrast white type, a single electric accent, OLED-friendly black. This is a native app, not a website in a shell — one-handed, fast, gesture-driven. Content leads with imagery floating on the black; blue is spent carefully. It is deliberately not a generic college app, not a cluttered Eventbrite feed, and not a corporate ticketing utility. The ticket is sacred: legible, resilient, and instantly scannable at a gate on a bad connection.
keyCharacteristics: True-black #000000 OLED canvas; high-contrast white type
Unifesto blue gradient as the one glowing accent
Mobile-first, one-handed, native gestures and large touch targets
Image-led content floating on black; blue spent sparingly
Resilient by design — the ticket/QR works even on poor connectivity

rules.name: The One Point of Light Rule
rules.body: On a black screen the blue accent is precious. Spend it on the primary action, the live indicator, and selection — not decoration. Its glow only works if it's rare.

rules.name: The Contrast-on-Black Rule
rules.body: Every text and icon meets WCAG AA against #000000. Muted grays are for secondary content only; nothing critical relies on low-contrast gray.

rules.name: The One Type Voice Rule
rules.body: Agrandir does the whole hierarchy through weight and size. Sweet Apricot stays in the logo.

rules.name: The Tonal-Depth Rule
rules.body: On black, elevation is a lighter shade of black plus a hairline border — not a heavy drop shadow. The only real glow belongs to the blue accent.

dos: Do keep the canvas true black #000000 — premium, OLED-friendly, and the whole point.
Do spend the blue accent sparingly: primary action, live indicator, selection.
Do meet WCAG AA contrast against black for every text and icon.
Do design one-handed: large touch targets, thumb-reachable actions, native gestures.
Do lead with imagery floating on the black.
Do make the ticket/QR resilient — legible offline, cached, instantly scannable; treat it as sacred.
donts: Don't ship a generic college app or a cluttered Eventbrite-style feed.
Don't feel like a ported website — use native motion and gestures.
Don't overuse blue; if the whole screen glows, nothing does.
Don't rely on low-contrast gray for anything critical.
Don't add a second type family beyond Agrandir (Sweet Apricot stays in the logo).
Don't put the ticket/QR behind a required network call or a spinner it can get stuck on.
